title: Generalizable Prediction of Mixture Etching Rates Using Graph Neural Networks
experiments_summary: The study uses a physics-based model (PBM) of the GEC reference reactor in inductively coupled plasma (ICP) mode to generate etching rate data for pure O2, pure Ar, and their mixtures etching PMMA blanket samples. Operating conditions span pressures of 10–70 mTorr and varying coil powers. The proposed architecture consists of two pre-trained single-chemistry feedforward neural networks (one for O2, one for Ar) whose weights are frozen during mixture training. Normalized power and pressure inputs are passed through these networks, and their outputs (or intermediate layer representations) are concatenated with the corresponding gas fraction to form node feature vectors. These vectors populate a two-node complete directed graph (one node per gas), processed by a GraphSAGE layer followed by ReLU activation and a linear output layer predicting 10 etching rates. The framework is evaluated on two test sets: a grid-based test set (Test_grid) and a threshold-based test set (Test_thresh). An ablation study investigates four different node feature representations extracted from different layers of the pre-trained networks: (i) final network outputs, (ii) last hidden layer, (iii) second-to-last hidden layer, and (iv) first hidden layer. The GraphSAGE-based model is compared against a feedforward neural network (FNN) baseline and also benchmarked against a GAT-based variant, with the hidden dimension of the GraphSAGE layer tuned to match the baseline parameter count for fair comparison.
